A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same asymmetric zigzag sampling work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite the changed title and appendix organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original SDXL and FLUX experiments, visual-injection and token-selection ablations, generated examples, and a 20-participant preference study.

after.justification: V4 retains those empirical results and adds a prompt-conditioning ablation, inference-time measurements, and a long-story demonstration.

M1.justification: V4 adds a sliding-window inference extension for long stories in Section 5. The core visual-token caching, zig-only injection, null-prompt zag step, and one-prompt/IPCA guidance already appear in v1; Algorithms 1–2 primarily document that existing procedure.

E1.justification: The existing benchmark coverage remains, while v4 adds a long-narrative scenario requiring consistency across prompt windows, illustrated by 42 FLUX images in Appendix G. Several subjects newly featured in the main comparisons already appeared in v1's appendices, so those substitutions do not establish new domains.

E2.justification: The named external baseline sets remain unchanged for SDXL, FLUX, and the user study. New Table 4 adds an explicitly evaluated symmetric-prompt control against the proposed asymmetric configuration; v1's tabulated symmetry comparisons varied visual injection instead.

E3.justification: V4 adds a controlled comparison of full versus null prompt conditioning during zag and a per-image latency evaluation at 50 SDXL and 28 FLUX sampling steps. Existing benchmark metrics, background preprocessing, sampling budgets, and user-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds an ablation testing the contribution of asymmetric prompt conditioning and an analysis measuring computational overhead. The visual-injection scheduling and top-k sensitivity analyses are retained; v1 Table 4 becomes v4 Table 5 without changed results.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the statement about using previously reported random seeds. Neither reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v4 adds no uncertainty estimates for its new ablation or timing measurements.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables are unchanged. V4 adds prompt-ablation results, revised qualitative examples, a long-story output, and timings of 21.33 versus 7.44 seconds for SDXL and 5.50 versus 1.50 seconds for FLUX. New Table 4 lists asymmetric CLIP-T/CLIP-I as 0.923/0.8946, reversed relative to the retained full-model rows; its accompanying prose gives DreamSim 0.1789 whereas the table gives 0.1798.

T1.justification: The diffusion loss, denoising and inverse-denoising equations, attention-score definitions, and token-concatenation mathematics are retained. The added pseudocode restates the existing procedure rather than introducing new theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free asymmetric zigzag sampling improves subject consistency while preserving prompt alignment and works with SDXL and FLUX. The revised title and clearer attribution of one-prompt guidance do not change those claims.

C2.justification: V4 interprets the method as test-time scaling, discusses measured latency as a quality-cost tradeoff, and extends its claimed applicability to long narratives. Appendix B adds specific privacy, impersonation, and misinformation risks and suggested safeguards. The existing computational and SDXL limitations are moved into Section 7 without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds algorithm listings for identity-token caching and the sampling loop, and Section 5 supplies inference times. Model versions, guidance scales, injection layers, A100 hardware, baseline implementation instructions, and the code link remain unchanged. The long-story extension does not specify window size or overlap.

R1.justification: V4 adds the Neuralflix citation to the introductory brain-signal examples and relates its long-story extension to One-Prompt-One-Story. The main related-work discussion and positioning against existing consistency methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 revises the title, repairs an incomplete personalization description, clarifies terminology, and renames the visual-injection ablation. It moves limitations into the main text, adds acknowledgements, and reorganizes appendix headings. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds the prompt-ablation table, two boxed algorithm listings, and long-story Figure 10. Figure 3 gains sampling-stage labels, Figures 4 and 6 substitute qualitative examples, and Figure 9 changes selected outputs. Existing grid designs and most table layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 modestly improves practical assessment by quantifying previously only acknowledged inference overhead, demonstrating a long-story extension, and discussing concrete societal risks. The new prompt ablation offers additional evidence, but its reversed CLIP values and DreamSim discrepancy weaken that contribution. The core benchmark results remain unchanged, so the gains are limited rather than a substantial strengthening of the paper.
